$comment: How the committed catalogue is known to be the pinned revisions' catalogue. Three independent facts per source: (1) the binary that produced the committed capture stamps the commit it was built from, and that commit's build inputs are byte-identical to the pin; (2) a fresh release build made from `git archive <pin>` emits a canonically identical tools/list result; (3) the archive and both binaries are hashed. Read-only: no source repository was modified.
method: git -C <repo> diff --stat <binary-stamp-commit> <pin> -- src Cargo.toml Cargo.lock build.rs  (expect empty: identical build inputs)
git -C <repo> archive --format=tar -o <tar> <pin>  (read-only export; no worktree, no index change)
tar -xf <tar> -C <dir>; cargo build --release --locked --offline  (pinned toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml)
compare: tools/list canonical hash of the pin build vs the installed binary

gladius.pinSubject: docs(gladius): link the enabled issue tracker

sourceIdentity.reading: the installed binary's build inputs are byte-identical to the pin

pinVsHead.command: git diff --stat 59c6d77 HEAD -- src Cargo.toml Cargo.lock build.rs tests
pinVsHead.reading: no src/, manifest, lockfile or build.rs change since the pin; only a test's claim text moved

limits: A catalogue is not a behaviour guarantee: the tool schemas, descriptions and annotations are pinned, not the handlers. Runtime semantics, typed error codes, deadlines and safety behaviour are covered by each project's own tests, not by this baseline.

No tool was called during capture. initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, tools/list (legacy and 2026-07-28 `_meta`) and server/discover are the only methods sent, so no browser was launched and no desktop was touched.
Only tools/list is captured. prompts/list, resources/list and logging are not advertised by either server's capabilities and were not probed.

The pin-built binary reports `unknown-dirty` because build.rs runs git inside a directory of this uncommitted repo; identity rests on the archive hash and the two build-input diffs, not on that stamp.

The archive hash was reproduced byte-identically by re-running `git archive` on this machine (git 2.56.0.windows.4). A different git version may write a different pax header, so the hash identifies the tree as exported here, not a universal constant.
